news.title: James and Russo lead rout of Greece as ruthless England set up Ukraine playoff
news.lede: Playoff semi-final second leg: England 5-0 Greece (agg 8-1). Goalscorers: Russo 3 75, James 16 34, Stanway 30. A mercurial Lauren James scored two and provided an assist in a thrilling four-goal first 45 minutes against Greece, as England put themselves two games away from securing their place at the World Cup. James’s double was matched by Alessia Russo, who scored either side of the break, and her Arsenal ­teammate Georgia Stanway was also on the scoresheet, with the Lionesses setting up a playoff final against Ukraine in November and December.

news.title: Potter helps England find magic but World Cup playoff format needs rethink | Tom Garry
news.lede: Lexi Potter and Lauren James stole the show against Greece but England’s 8-1 aggregate win was one of many lopsided scorelines. If there had been a vidiprinter at the King Power Stadium displaying the aggregate scorelines from the night’s Women’s World Cup qualifying playoffs around Europe, it might have looked more at home on the cricket scoreboard just over a mile further south at Leicestershire’s Grace Road. Sweden 15-0 against Lithuania. Republic of Ireland 12-0 against Kazakhstan.

news.title: England 5-0 Greece (8-1 on aggregate): Alessia Russo, Lauren James star as Lionesses cruise into World Cup play-offs second round
news.lede: Alessia Russo and Lauren James reiterated their importance to England as both scored twice in a 5-0 win against Greece in the second leg of their World Cup play-off first-round tie, winning 8-1 on aggregate. In fact, it was the Chelsea forward who supplied the Arsenal No 9 for an early opener - needed after a laborious 3-1 in Crete on Friday gave the Lionesses plenty to consider. But once England had taken the lead at the King Power Stadium they did not look back. James doubled the hosts' lead with a rocket effort before Georgia Stanway's bullet header made it three after Lauren Hemp's cross.

news.title: Lexi Potter: England Women midfielder the present, not just the future after impressive debut in World Cup play-off
news.lede: Lexi Potter could not have done more to prove she should not only be in England’s World Cup squad next summer, she could also be in the starting XI. It's a big shout for a player that's only just broken into the England team, but her 60-minute debut against Greece couldn't have gone much better. "It was really special," the Chelsea midfielder told ITV Sport after the game. "I am very happy and proud.

news.title: Katie McCabe Issued Rallying Cry To Ireland Fans After World Cup Playoff Final Place Secured
news.lede: Katie McCabe has sent a clear request to Ireland fans after the Girls in Green booked their place in the World Cup playoff final with another rout of Kazakhstan on Tuesday night. Ireland ran riot in last Friday's 8-0 win in Astana, but this was a bit more of a challenge for Carla Ward's troops, as they found it difficult to break down a more stubborn Kazakh defence. Recommended They finally made their first-half pressure pay with Jessie Stapleton's header shortly before half-time, and the floodgates began to open after the break. For the first time in Cork, McCabe was on the scoresheet, rifling home from just outside the box shortly after the break.

news.title: Republic of Ireland 4-0 Kazakhstan (agg 12-0): We have to 'lock in' for World Cup dream - Katie McCabe
news.lede: Katie McCabe scored in Cork as the Republic of Ireland booked their place in the final play-off round. The final whistle had just blown in Cork, but Katie McCabe's mind was already six weeks ahead. Eight goals to the good from Friday, the second leg of the Women's World Cup play-off with Kazakhstan was always going to be an easy night for the Republic of Ireland. There were another four goals on the night, including a powerful strike from McCabe, and it leaves Carla Ward's side just two matches away from the 2027 Women's World Cup.

news.title: Women's World Cup play-off final: Pressure on Norway, says Wales boss Rhian Wilkinson
news.lede: Wales are through to a second successive Women's World Cup play-off final. Rhian Wilkinson says the pressure will be on Gemma Grainger's Norway in their Women's World Cup play-off final against Wales in December. Wales moved a step closer to reaching the Women's World Cup for the first time as a 3-0 win over Albania in Llanelli secured a 4-0 aggregate success in their play-off semi-final. Wales now face a step up in a class as they take on a Norway side ranked 14th in the world, but Wilkinson insists Wales can "absolutely" cause an upset as they are reunited with former boss Grainger.
